classification.difficultyReason: Construct two graphs on common axes, identify the absolute-value branches, and interpret their intersections as equation solutions; the parts explicitly guide each representation change.

children.label: a
children.prompt: On the same set of axes, sketch $y=|x-2|$ and $y=\dfrac{x}{3}$.

answer.short: The graphs are shown on common axes.
answer.worked: The graph of $y=|x-2|$ has vertex $(2,0)$ and passes through $(0,2)$ and $(4,2)$. The line $y=\dfrac{x}{3}$ passes through $(0,0)$ and $(3,1)$. Draw both on the same axes.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the equations of the branches of $y=|x-2|$, and label them on your diagram.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-(x-2)=-x+2&& (x<2),\\y&=x-2&& (x\geq2).\end{align*}$$
Label the left branch $y=-x+2$ and the right branch $y=x-2$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Explain how the solutions of the equation $|x-2|=\dfrac{x}{3}$ are represented on your diagram.

answer.short: They are the $x$-coordinates of the intersection points.
answer.worked: At an intersection, both graphs have the same $y$-value, so $|x-2|=\dfrac{x}{3}$. The $x$-coordinates of those intersections are the solutions.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Hence, find the solutions of the equation $|x-2|=\dfrac{x}{3}$.

answer.worked:
The intersections are $\left(\dfrac32,\dfrac12\right)$ and $(3,1)$. Their $x$-coordinates give $x=\dfrac32$ or $x=3$.
The branch equations confirm the exact coordinates:
$$\begin{align*}-x+2&=\frac{x}{3},\\2&=\frac{4x}{3},\\x&=\frac32;\\x-2&=\frac{x}{3},\\\frac{2x}{3}&=2,\\x&=3.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: One shared set of axes for the absolute value graph, line, branch labels and intersections. Blue and red distinguish the two equations.
spec.mathematics: y=|x-2| and y=x/3 intersect at (3/2,1/2) and (3,1).
